blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British offices usually deal with conflict calmly and behind closed doors. Shouting is very rare. When colleagues disagree, they book a one-to-one coffee. They do not argue in front of the team.

If things get tense, lower your voice, stay polite, and listen longer than you speak. Look for a shared path forward. Public confrontation is embarrassing — even when the other person is clearly wrong.

Quiet resolution is, for most British offices, a sign of professionalism.

items.q: How do British offices usually deal with conflict?
items.why: "British offices usually deal with conflict calmly and behind closed doors."

items.q: When colleagues disagree, what do they do?
items.why: "When colleagues disagree, they book a one-to-one coffee."

items.q: If things get tense, what should you do?
options: Lower your voice and stay polite
items.why: "lower your voice, stay polite, and listen longer than you speak."

items.q: The text suggests that shouting in a British office is…
items.why: Inferência: se calma é profissionalismo, gritar é o contrário — visto como pouco profissional.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A shared path forward is a good goal.
It is better to correct someone in public.
You should listen more than you speak.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que confronto público é constrangedor — corrigir alguém em público é o oposto do conselho.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando o gerente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, you have two strong people on your team, and they disagree. That is normal. It happens in every office. But please, do not fix it in front of everyone. That only makes it worse.

Here is my advice. Talk to each of them alone, first. Book a quiet coffee, one to one. Ask them what they really want. Then listen. Listen longer than you speak. You will learn a lot.

Later, when they talk to each other, stay calm. If the room gets tense, lower your voice. A calm voice helps everyone. Do not shout, and do not take a side too fast. Be fair. Give both people time to speak.

Remember, your job is not to pick a winner. Your job is to find a shared path forward. Look for something that both of them can accept. Not perfect, but good enough for the team.

And do all of this behind closed doors. Never in the open office. If you sort it out quietly, the team will trust you more. Here in Britain, that quiet, calm way is a sign of a good manager. That is how we do it here.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie say about the disagreement between the two people?
items.why: "two strong people on your team, and they disagree. That is normal."

items.q: How should the manager talk to each person first?
items.why: "Talk to each of them alone. Book a quiet coffee, one to one."

items.q: What should the manager do if the room gets tense?
items.why: "If the room gets tense, lower your voice."

items.q: Sophie says the manager's job is NOT to…
items.why: "Your job is not to pick a winner."

items.q: Why does Sophie want the manager to sort it out quietly?
options: Because it is a company rule
Because the team will trust him more
items.why: Inferência: "If you sort it out quietly, the team will trust you more." — a calma constrói confiança.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "There is a conflict between the two teams." A conflict is…
items.why: Conflict = conflito, um desacordo sério.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The room felt ___ when the two managers stopped talking."
items.why: Tense = tenso; combina com o clima pesado da sala.

items.q: "They talked behind closed doors." This means they talked…
items.why: Behind closed doors = a portas fechadas, em privado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A ___ meeting is just you and one other person."
items.why: One-to-one = individual, só duas pessoas.

items.q: "It was embarrassing to argue in front of everyone." Embarrassing means…
items.why: Embarrassing = constrangedor, que causa vergonha.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando lidamos com conflito no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's sort out this problem quietly." To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, arrumar o problema.

items.q: "One colleague pushed back on the plan." This means she…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "Please calm down before the meeting." To calm down means to…
items.why: Calm down = acalmar-se, ficar tranquilo.

items.q: "They finally made up after the argument." To make up means to…
items.why: Make up = fazer as pazes depois de uma briga.

items.q: "Let's talk it over in private." To talk it over means to…
items.why: Talk it over = conversar sobre algo com calma para resolver.
